feed.title: Smart Glasses & Wearables — Useful Sites
feed.subtitle: An annotated directory of links on software, AI, security and science. Every entry states what the resource does and where it parts ways with its neighbours.

entry.title: Meta Ray-Ban Display
entry.summary: Meta’s display glasses controlled by an EMG wristband. A closed ecosystem, but a reference point for where the input method is heading.

entry.title: Brilliant Labs
entry.summary: A glasses maker that publishes both hardware schematics and software — close to the only company in the sector selling a product while opening the design.

entry.title: Açık Kaynak Gözlük Yaptık
entry.summary: A video on building open-source glasses that is honest about which parts are genuinely hard. Worth watching before committing to the project.

entry.title: Akıllı Gözlük Yapımı
entry.summary: A step-by-step build starting from components rather than a kit. The optical combiner and power management sections are the hard parts.

entry.title: GitHub · ray-ban-meta
entry.summary: Community projects around Ray-Ban Meta glasses. With no official SDK, the work here is mostly protocol analysis and unofficial bridges.

entry.title: Açık Kaynak Gözlük Yapımı
entry.summary: A step-by-step build guide with a bill of materials and assembly order — exactly the level of detail that makes a project reproducible.

entry.title: Mentra Bluetooth SDK
entry.summary: A starter kit for connecting to glasses over BLE from Android. GATT services and characteristics arrive defined, so you do not reverse-engineer the protocol yourself.

entry.title: MentraOS
entry.summary: An open operating system for smart glasses unifying different vendors’ hardware under one app layer — aimed at the problem of writing a separate app per device.

entry.title: Omi
entry.summary: A wearable that listens to conversations and summarises them, capturing context rather than vision. The ethics of always-on listening are a separate argument.

entry.title: OpenGlass
entry.summary: Converts an existing pair of glasses by attaching a camera and board, on a parts list of roughly $25. Conversion rather than manufacture.

entry.title: Open Source Smart Glasses
entry.summary: An all-day wearable open-source glasses design with schematics, PCB and software published — so unlike closed products you can see what it collects and where it sends it.

entry.title: GitHub · smart-glasses
entry.summary: A live list of tagged open-source projects that stays current by itself, unlike curated lists — the way to catch new arrivals.

entry.title: HeyCyan Wi-Fi Aktarım Mimarisi
entry.summary: A technical note on how media transfer from glasses to phone is structured — control over BLE, bulk data over Wi-Fi. A pattern directly applicable to similar devices.

entry.title: HeyCyan Web Köprüsü
entry.summary: Connects the glasses to a browser over Web Bluetooth, so you can talk to the device without writing a native app — a fast route for prototyping.

entry.title: Alternatif HeyCyan Uygulaması
entry.summary: An open-source alternative to the vendor app, aimed at unlocking restricted features and removing the cloud dependency.

entry.title: HeyCyan SDK
entry.summary: A cross-platform SDK for HeyCyan glasses giving application-level control over photo, video and audio capture.

entry.title: Brilliant Labs Halo
entry.summary: AI glasses where a developer can load their own applications — unlike closed ecosystems, the right to run code on the device is yours.

entry.title: Akıllı Gözlük İşletim Sistemleri
entry.summary: A comparison of Horizon OS, Android XR and the rest. Which ecosystem to invest in is a decision that precedes hardware selection.

entry.title: Giyilebilir Yonga Setleri
entry.summary: An article on the graphics-versus-power trade-off in high-end wearables. In display glasses, the GPU choice sets battery life directly.

entry.title: PSOC4 CAPSENSE Uygulama Notu
entry.summary: An application note on adding touch control to a glasses temple, with circuit diagram and calibration parameters. Documentation this concrete is rarely public.

entry.title: RealMCU Akıllı Gözlük
entry.summary: A vendor offering low-power glasses silicon aimed at simpler, cheaper devices than Qualcomm. For glasses that only show notifications, a Snapdragon is overkill.

entry.title: Qualcomm AI Glasses
entry.summary: The official page for the Snapdragon AR platform found in most shipping glasses, holding the reference designs and power figures.

entry.title: Akıllı Gözlük Yonga Rehberi
entry.summary: A comparison of processors and NPUs used in glasses, weighing power budget and thermal limits — in a frame the real constraint is heat, not compute.

entry.title: Even G2 Protokolü
entry.summary: Reverse-engineering of the device’s BLE protocol — the only route to uses the official SDK does not permit.

entry.title: Awesome Even Realities G2
entry.summary: A community resource collection for the G2, accumulating the tools and solved problems the official documentation does not cover.

entry.title: Even Realities (GitHub)
entry.summary: The vendor’s official repositories and the primary source for the SDK and sample apps. A hardware maker publishing code is still the exception in this sector.

entry.title: Even Hub
entry.summary: The vendor’s developer hub, holding app development resources and API documentation.

entry.title: Even Realities · Çerçeve Seçimi
entry.summary: Frame and prescription lens options — the part that decides whether the glasses actually get worn daily, more than the technology does.

entry.title: Even Realities G2
entry.summary: Everyday glasses with a display and deliberately no camera. The omission is a decision rather than a shortfall — it addresses the social acceptance problem head on.
